title: Leaf / cactus stem cross-section with a pore (drawn)
depicts: Drawn leaf / cactus-stem cross-section: a pore between guard cells, CO2 in, water vapour out; C3 tall cells, C4 rings round a vein, CAM night store.

licence.author: Reel Studio (in-house illustration)
licence.changes: source: remotion/v3/components/LeafSection.tsx (meta src/v3/components-meta/LeafSection.ts); a generic textbook-style leaf section drawn in-house, not traced from any figure

leaf.label: the leaf, cut open
leaf.physical: a leaf cut through to show the cells inside (illustration, not to scale)

pore.label: a pore (stoma)
pore.physical: a tiny opening on the underside: carbon dioxide gets in and water vapour gets out through it

guards.label: the guard cells
guards.physical: two cells either side of the pore that open and close it

inside.label: the air inside
inside.physical: the air space just inside the pore

co2.in.label: carbon dioxide coming in
co2.in.physical: carbon dioxide from the air, drifting in through the pore

water.out.label: water vapour going out
water.out.physical: water vapour leaving through the same pore

skin.label: the waxy skin
skin.physical: the top skin with its waxy layer (keeps water in)

outer.label: the outer cells
outer.physical: they grab the carbon dioxide first and pass it inward

outer.cell.label: an outer cell
outer.cell.physical: grabs carbon dioxide and passes it inward as a 4-carbon acid

inner.label: the inner cells
inner.physical: the ring round the vein where the carbon dioxide is handed over and the sugar is made

inner.cell.label: an inner cell
inner.cell.physical: gets the carbon dioxide handed in and makes the sugar

vein.label: the vein
vein.physical: carries water in and the sugar away

handoff.label: the handoff
handoff.physical: the outer cells passing the carbon dioxide inward (as a 4-carbon acid)

sugar.label: where the sugar is made
sugar.physical: the inner ring round the vein

sky.label: day or night
sky.physical: the sun by day, the moon at night
